items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Could you hold one price for seventy years? Coca-Cola did. A Coke cost five cents through two world wars. Why couldn't it rise?
In eighteen ninety-nine, two lawyers got Coke's bottling rights, with the syrup price fixed permanently.
So why not just charge more?
Coke tied its brand to five cents, and its vending machines took a single nickel. The next coin up was a dime, double the price.
And that's not even the strangest part.
Coke asked the U.S. Treasury for a seven-and-a-half-cent coin. Its boss even asked his hunting buddy, President Eisenhower. The answer was no.
Inflation finally won. By nineteen fifty-nine, the nickel Coke was gone.
The price never moved. Your nickel just kept getting weaker.
[smug, deep, rich, self-satisfied] Should've priced it in gold.
Comment: what price do you wish never changed?
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
